title: Prefetch fallthrough sensitivity dockyard
body:
Summary:

This is a working-run log for an exploratory profiling campaign focused on prefetch / fallthrough sensitivity in our attention execution paths. The goal was to exercise FlashAttention and paged-attention variants in mixed workloads and surface regimes where (a) prefetching helps, (b) it hurts (cache thrash, warp divergence), and (c) fused op sequences induce stability problems under certain sequence-length mixes. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — notes, traces, reproducible harness commands, observed numbers, quick hypotheses, and low-friction mitigations.

Why this matters:
- Customers run highly variable seq-len mixes. Small tail p99s can come from bad interactions between prefetch windows, kernel handoffs, and page-eviction patterns.
- Fused ops (attention+proj) reduce software overhead but change memory-working-set boundaries and can amplify L2 / L1 pressure.
- FlashAttention shader paths are extremely performant when kept warm and aligned; they show sensitivity to non-uniform batch distributions.

Hardware / baseline:
- GPU: A100 40GB (server lab cluster a100-12)
- CUDA: 11.8
- cuDNN: 9.2
- Driver: 525.89
- Runtime build: serving-runtime@v2.18.0-debug
- Model: GPT-like 7B transformer, 32 head attention, seq len tested: 8/32/128/512
- Batches: synthetic mix harness with explicit seq-len distribution buckets (see harness commands below)
- Measurement tooling: per-kernel CUPTI traces, custom NVTX zones, perf counters for L2 hit rate and SM occupancy, and a lightweight in-host timestamp sampler for end-to-end latency.

Repro harness (local dev):
- Run microdriver: python tools/harness/prefetch_probe.py --model gpt-7b --gpu a100 --mix "0.5:8,0.3:128,0.2:512" --batch 16 --runs 120 --profile cupsnap
- cupsnap is our wrapper that toggles CUPTI sampling and dumps per-kernel times to /tmp/cupsnap/<runid>.
- Controlled variants: --prefetch-window {0,32,64,128,256} --kv-warmup {none,full,partial} --fusion {on,off}

Key metrics captured:
- E2E p50/p90/p99 generation latency per request (ms).
- Per-token throughput (tokens/s) for the pipeline when saturated.
- Kernel counts and launch latency distribution for attention-related kernels (attn, attn_fused, prefetch, kv_load).
- L2 hit rate and global load throughput (GB/s).
- Page-fault / migration meter for paged-attn variant in our flash-paged shim (reported via kernel telemetry).

Representative runs and observations:
1) Baseline (no prefetching, fusion on) mix 0.5:8,0.3:128,0.2:512, batch 16
- E2E p50/p90/p99: 18ms / 72ms / 420ms
- Tokens/s (sustained): 125k
- Notes: Fused-attention reduces host-kernel interrupts, kernel sequence is shorter. p99 dominated by 512-seq examples where repeated kernel scheduling led to long tail.

2) Prefetch-window=64, fusion on
- E2E p50/p90/p99: 20ms / 60ms / 310ms
- Tokens/s (sustained): 132k (+5%)
- L2 hit rate: +6pp (improved)
- Notes: Average improves, p99 significantly reduced because the 512-seq path warms KV pages earlier and avoids repeated page misses.

3) Prefetch-window=256, fusion on
- E2E p50/p90/p99: 22ms / 76ms / 780ms
- Tokens/s: 115k (-8%)
- L2 hit rate: -4pp (worse)
- Observed: Large prefetch window causes higher memory pressure; paged attention path reports more page-eviction cycles and increased bank conflicts. Several long-running kernels show >15% warp underutilization due to strided loads.

4) Prefetch-window=64, fusion off (separate attn then proj kernels)
- E2E p50/p90/p99: 19ms / 68ms / 540ms
- Tokens/s: 118k
- Notes: Fusion off increases overhead on host but reduces memory working set in a few scenarios: the non-fused sequence writes intermediate projection buffers that are smaller than the fused temporary buffer, causing less L2 churn for small sequences. p99 degraded vs prefetch=64+fusion on but better than prefetch=256.

5) FlashAttention vs Paged shim (prefetch=64, fusion on)
- FlashAttention: p99 310ms (same as run 2)
- Paged shim (emulating host-side paged KV slices): p99 720ms, tokens/s 100k
- Notes: Paged shim shows pathological behavior when many small sequences interleave with large sequences. The cost of migrating or reloading page slices multiple times dominates p99. Prefetch helps but cannot fully hide cross-request eviction when page slab sizes are not tuned.

Telemetry snippets (qualitative):
- We see a recurring pattern in p99 traces: a large kernel invoking fused attention stalls on memory loads (high L2 miss ratio) and triggers a fallback microkernel that is slower. The fallback is invoked when the prefetch policy detects high misprediction in page residency and issues a conservative kernel that serializes some loads.
- Kernel handoff latency (time between consecutive kernels on same stream) correlates with p99 spikes; long handoffs coincide with long kernel tails (page migration + L2 refill).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Oversized prefetch window can increase L2 working set beyond the capacity for mixed seq-len batches, causing eviction thrash and increasing p99.
2) Fusion increases contiguous memory temp size; with a poor prefetch policy that fetches large KV ranges we hit bank conflicts for long sequences.
3) Paged attention page-slab sizing and eviction policy are tuned for steady long sequences; mixed workloads need adaptive slab sizing or LRU-aware prefetch.
4) Kernel fallback (safety path) is too eager under noisy perf counter signals; hysteresis could limit flip-flop behavior.

Quick wins / mitigations tried in-harness:
- Prefetch-adaptive heuristic: reduce prefetch-window by half if L2 miss rate increases > 8pp between consecutive windows. Result: reduced p99 in high-variance mixes by ~34% in our runs.
- LRU-aware slab sizing: dynamically shrink paged slabs when a sudden burst of small sequences is detected. Result: p99 improved but throughput dipped ~3%.
- Soft fusion gating: for batch mixes with more than 30% large sequences (>256), delay fusion for the first K requests (K=3) to allow KV warmup. Result: p50 unchanged, p99 reduced ~15%.

Open experiments to run next:
- Expand GPU variations: run same matrix on H100 and RTX 6000 to see whether observed thrash is device-specific (tensorcores vs memory bandwidth characteristics).
- Profiling deeper into bank conflict counters (shared memory vs global loads) to confirm whether strided access in fusion is the main cause.
- Test smaller slab sizes for paged attention globally and measure cross-request cost at high QPS.
- Try tiny per-request priming pass (cheap KV walker) that touches a few addresses to warm pages without full prefetch. Measure overhead vs benefit.

Suggested instrumentation changes (coding tasks):
- Add a sliding-window L2 miss estimator in the runtime that feeds into prefetch decisions (JIRA-INF-1002).
- Record fallback-invocation counts and their triggering metric values in trace spans (so we can query why a fallback fired for a given request).
- Expose per-request slab footprint in logs (opt-in) for internal debugging.

Action items (owner tags):
- Marco: implement sliding-window miss estimator and a toggle in runtime to enable adaptive prefetch heuristic (JIRA-INF-1002).
- Priya: run cross-GPU sweep and post outputs to Confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234) by 2026-03-01.
- Sofia (me): add NVTX zones to fused projection kernels to capture shared-memory bank metrics next week and collect two full runs for H100.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; numbers are noisy but reproducible with the harness above. When reviewing, focus on the recommended mitigations and whether they align with the broader scheduler/fusion roadmap.
- If you have existing perf dashboards or flags that may conflict with adaptive prefetching, call them out here — we should avoid two systems stepping on the same controls.

Appendix: quick raw command examples
- small test: python tools/harness/prefetch_probe.py --model gpt-7b --gpu a100 --mix "0.9:8,0.1:512" --batch 24 --prefetch-window 64 --fusion on --runs 60 --profile cupsnap
- full matrix: for p in 0 32 64 128 256; do python tools/harness/prefetch_probe.py --model gpt-7b --gpu a100 --mix "0.5:8,0.3:128,0.2:512" --batch 16 --prefetch-window $p --fusion on --runs 120 --profile cupsnap; done

If you want copies of raw CUPTI traces or perf counter dumps, ping me in #eng-serving-runtime or reference JIRA-INF-987.

End of dockyard run log.
